title: Multi-View Causal Discovery without Non-Gaussianity: Identifiability and Algorithms
claim: Shared causal ordering across views is recovered first by iteratively finding roots, then view-specific weights are estimated.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, brace linking ground-truth views to learning steps
description: Three rounded panels with titles on their top borders, read left to right. The left panel, 'Ground-truth', shows stacked views (View 1, an ellipsis for View i, View m). Each view is the same five-node DAG with colored circles (orange, blue, red, green, purple) and gray edge weights that differ between views. A large curly brace links this panel to the next two. The middle panel, 'Learning: Step 1', shows the graph being built step by step along arrows: it starts with a single orange root, then adds nodes and edges until the full ordering is recovered. A gray caption reads 'Iteratively find a root variable'. The right panel, 'Learning: Step 2', repeats the views with re-estimated weights and the caption 'Estimate weights'. The eye goes first to the colored DAGs.
caption: Left panel: Visual representation of our multi-view LiMVAM model in Eq. 3. Each view of the data is described by a causal graph, nodes represent variables, and disturbances are not illustrated. We see that the causal ordering given by the DAGs is shared over views 1 . . . m, but causal weights can differ. Middle and right panels: Main steps of the PairwiseLiMVAM and DirectLiMVAM algorithms. In Step 1, the shared causal ordering is progressively determined. In Step 2, view-specific causal weights are estimated.
abstract: Causal discovery is a difficult problem that typically relies on strong assumptions on the data-generating model, such as non-Gaussianity. In practice, many modern applications provide multiple related views of the same system, which has rarely been considered for causal discovery. Here, we leverage this multi-view structure to achieve causal discovery with weak assumptions. We propose a multi-view linear Structural Equation Model (SEM) that extends the well-known framework of non-Gaussian disturbances by alternatively leveraging correlation over views. We prove the identifiability of the model for acyclic SEMs. Subsequently, we propose several multi-view causal discovery algorithms, inspired by single-view algorithms (DirectLiNGAM, PairwiseLiNGAM, and ICA-LiNGAM). The new methods are validated through simulations and applications on neuroimaging data, where they enable the estimation of causal graphs between brain regions.
